summary: Account Edit feature tested: PUT /api/accounts/{id} works correctly for all field updates (code/name/type/parentId/balance). UI Edit modal opens, shows all fields, allows editing. Minor frontend Response parsing bug causes error message but API update works.

ui_bugs.issue: Response body parsing error: 'Failed to execute clone on Response: Response body is already used'. The error appears in the modal but the actual PUT request succeeds.
ui_bugs.root_cause: In updateAccountById function, response.json().catch(() => ({})) pattern may conflict with subsequent response.ok check. The frontend tries to read the response body after it has already been consumed.

action_items: Fix Response body parsing bug in ChartOfAccounts.jsx: updateAccountById function. The response.json().catch() pattern causes issues. Suggested fix: Clone the response before parsing or use a single json() call with proper error handling.
critical_code_review_comments: ChartOfAccounts.jsx line 198: response.json().catch(() => ({})) combined with subsequent response.ok check causes 'Response body already used' error. Fix: const data = await response.json(); if (!response.ok) throw new Error(data?.detail || ...);

success_rate.frontend: 90% (Edit modal works, minor Response parsing bug)

seed_data_creation: Created TEST* prefixed accounts during testing. Cleaned up after tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Account edit feature is complete. Backend PUT /api/accounts/{id} works correctly. Frontend has minor Response parsing bug that shows error message but actual update succeeds. The trySmartAutoResolveUpdate fallback logic is implemented but wasn't triggered in tests since direct update worked.
rca_of_the_issue: Root cause: In updateAccountById(), the pattern response.json().catch(() => ({})) consumes the response body. When the code later checks response.ok (which succeeds), trying to access any response data again fails with 'Response body is already used'. This is a JavaScript Fetch API limitation - Response body can only be consumed once. Fix: Parse JSON first, then check status, or clone the response before parsing.
